decisions.rationale: Lead Gardevoir+Samurott-H both outspeed Farigiraf. Ceaseless Edge (69.6-130.3%) + Pixilate Hyper Voice (35.7-66.2%) guarantees Farigiraf KO before Trick Room. Samurott-H resists Camerupt Eruption. Back Incineroar+Kingambit for Intimidate pivoting and Dark STAB if TR goes up anyway.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 team: Incineroar/Kingambit/Gardevoir/Samurott-H. Opponent TR core: Farigiraf (Armor Tail/Mental Herb) + Mega Camerupt (Sheer Force). Armor Tail blocks all our priority. Key plan: lead Gardevoir+Samurott-H to double-target Farigiraf with Ceaseless Edge+Hyper Voice before TR. Both outspeed Sassy Farigiraf. Samurott-H Aqua Cutter threatens Camerupt after Farigiraf falls. Kingambit KowtowCleave is our hardest Farigiraf punish. Incineroar Parting Shot cycles to stall TR turns. Dragapult Shadow Ball immune to Farigiraf (Normal); Talonflame Gale Wings blocked by Armor Tail.

decisions.rationale: Lead Armor Tail Farigiraf plus Camerupt for reliable Trick Room pressure into the opponent’s common Tailwind/Parting Shot opening. Mawile supplies a powerful Trick Room Mega option, while Palafin gives an endgame pivot and priority Water pressure.
decisions.notebook: Opponent game-2 lead was Incineroar + Talonflame: Talonflame used turn-1 Tailwind while Incineroar used Parting Shot to bring Gardevoir. Incineroar repeatedly pivots with Parting Shot and cycles Intimidate. Talonflame has Tailwind, Taunt, Will-O-Wisp, Brave Bird; Armor Tail is especially valuable against it. Gardevoir has used Protect to stall Trick Room. Default plan: Farigiraf + Camerupt establish Trick Room, then apply Mega Camerupt pressure; Earth Power is the preferred Camerupt attack into Kingambit.

decisions.rationale: Gardevoir Mega Evolves for Pixilate Hyper Voice (32-60% to Farigiraf) + Samurott Ceaseless Edge (69-130% to Farigiraf). Combined min 101.8% guarantees KO on Farigiraf if it doesn't Protect, preventing Trick Room entirely. Both outspeed Farigiraf and Camerupt. If Farigiraf Protects, TR still isn't set and Hyper Voice chips Camerupt. Camerupt's Eruption cannot OHKO either mon without Helping Hand.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Gardevoir+Samurott-H lead vs Farigiraf+Camerupt TR. Gardevoir Mega Hyper Voice (Pixilate Fairy spread) + Samurott Ceaseless Edge double-targets Farigiraf to deny TR. Samurott Aqua Cutter OHKOs Camerupt (4x Water). Incineroar/Kingambit in back for cleanup. Farigiraf Armor Tail blocks our priority. Opponent's other 2 mons: Mawile (TR sweeper), Floette-Eternal, Palafin, or Liepard.

decisions.rationale: Preserve the Trick Room core by pivoting Farigiraf out of the obvious Gardevoir+Samurott double target. Mawile resists Pixilate Hyper Voice and Ceaseless Edge, while Camerupt’s Protect denies Samurott’s immediate Aqua Cutter pressure; retain Camerupt’s Mega option for a later Trick Room position.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s revealed Gardevoir is Timid Gardevoirite with Armor Tail pre-Mega and Pixilate after Mega; Hyper Voice, Psyshock, Mystical Fire, Protect. Hisuian Samurott is Adamant Chople Berry Sharpness with Ceaseless Edge, Aqua Cutter, Sacred Sword, Protect; Aqua Cutter is severe into Camerupt and Ceaseless Edge pressures Farigiraf. Opponent previously used Incineroar + Talonflame lead: Talonflame Tailwind/Taunt/Will-O-Wisp/Brave Bird and Incineroar Fake Out/Parting Shot/Will-O-Wisp/Flare Blitz with Sitrus Intimidate. Preserve Farigiraf for Trick Room; Mega Camerupt is the preferred TR sweeper, with Earth Power preferred into Kingambit. Mawile is a useful pivot into Fairy/Dark pressure and may be the alternate Mega.

decisions.rationale: Mawile Sucker Punch hits Gardevoir first (21-87% depending on Mega), but Gardevoir survives and Mystical Fire guarantees KO on 26% Mawile. Samurott Aqua Cutter outspeeds and OHKOs Camerupt before Eruption. Both foes eliminated this turn; Gardevoir lives to face Farigiraf + last mon with Samurott and backline intact.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Opponent brought Farigiraf, Camerupt, Mawile, and one of Floette-Eternal/Palafin/Liepard. Farigiraf has Armor Tail (blocks our priority). Camerupt-Mega has Sheer Force + Eruption/Heat Wave/Earth Power. Mawile-Mega has Huge Power + Play Rough (OHKOs Samurott-H). Camerupt 4x weak to Water; Aqua Cutter always OHKOs. Gardevoir-Mega Fairy Hyper Voice spread KOs low-HP Mawile through resist. Incineroar/Kingambit in back for cleanup; Kingambit Sucker Punch blocked by Armor Tail when Farigiraf is active.

decisions.rationale: Preserve Camerupt for a later Trick Room endgame and use Mawile’s intact Protect to buy Farigiraf a safe-ish entry. Farigiraf’s Armor Tail blocks priority and can establish Trick Room next turn; avoid committing the sole Mega to low-HP Mawile.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Gardevoir-Mega: Timid, Pixilate; Hyper Voice, Psyshock, Mystical Fire, Protect. Hisuian Samurott: Adamant Sharpness, Chople Berry; Ceaseless Edge, Aqua Cutter, Sacred Sword, Protect. Remaining possible opponents are Incineroar, Kingambit, Dragapult, Talonflame; previously seen Incineroar/Talonflame lead uses Fake Out/Parting Shot/Wisp/Flare Blitz and Tailwind/Taunt/Wisp/Brave Bird. Preserve Farigiraf to establish Trick Room where possible; Mega Camerupt is preferred TR win condition, especially Earth Power into Kingambit. Mawile pivots Fairy/Dark pressure but should not consume Mega if Camerupt TR sweep remains viable.

decisions.rationale: Hyper Voice spread KOs 26% Mawile guaranteed and chips Farigiraf; Ceaseless Edge into Farigiraf is a guaranteed KO from 35% with Sharpness boost. Both outspeed Farigiraf and KO before Trick Room resolves. Even if Farigiraf Protects, Mawile still falls, leaving us 2v1 with momentum.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Opponent brought Farigiraf, Camerupt, Mawile, and one of Floette-Eternal/Palafin/Liepard. Farigiraf has Armor Tail (blocks our priority targeting their side). Camerupt-Mega has Sheer Force + Eruption/Heat Wave/Earth Power. Mawile-Mega has Huge Power + Play Rough (OHKOs Samurott-H). Camerupt 4x weak to Water; Aqua Cutter always OHKOs. Gardevoir-Mega Fairy Hyper Voice spread KOs low-HP Mawile through resist. Kingambit Sucker Punch blocked by Armor Tail while Farigiraf active.

decisions.rationale: Intimidate drops both foes' Attack, giving Samurott-H a ~12% survival chance vs Play Rough. Flare Blitz always KOs 26% Mawile-Mega (min 66.2%). If Samurott lives, Ceaseless Edge always KOs 37% Palafin (min 37.7%). Even if Samurott faints, we remove Mawile and face Palafin + back line with Incineroar + Kingambit. Kingambit is safer defensively but cannot secure two KOs this turn and forfeits Intimidate value.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 decisive. Opponent brought Farigiraf (Armor Tail blocks priority for their side), Camerupt-Mega (Sheer Force Eruption/Heat Wave/Earth Power), Mawile-Mega (Huge Power, Play Rough OHKOs Samurott-H without Intimidate), and Palafin (Zero to Hero, Wave Crash 2HKOs Incineroar). Mawile Mega Evolved turn 3. Spikes are on opponent's side from our Ceaseless Edge. Our Gardevoir-Mega fainted turn 3 to Mawile Sucker Punch crit. Kingambit Sucker Punch is blocked when Farigiraf is active. Camerupt 4x weak to Water; Samurott Aqua Cutter always OHKOs. Incineroar Flare Blitz always KOs Mawile-Mega from 26%. Sitrus Berry on Incineroar unactivated.

decisions.rationale: Mega Sucker Punch gives immediate priority chip into Gardevoir if it attacks while preserving Farigiraf by switching it out. This avoids sacrificing Farigiraf before it can later establish Trick Room for Mega Camerupt; Palafin can absorb the expected Water-targeted attack more reliably than Camerupt.
decisions.notebook: Opponent revealed Mega Gardevoir (Timid Pixilate: Hyper Voice, Psyshock, Mystical Fire, Protect) and Adamant Sharpness Hisuian Samurott (Ceaseless Edge, Aqua Cutter, Sacred Sword, Protect; Chople Berry). Other possible reserves: Incineroar, Kingambit, Dragapult, Talonflame; only two are present. Preserve Farigiraf for a later Trick Room opportunity and keep Camerupt’s Mega available as the preferred TR win condition. Mega Mawile’s priority Sucker Punch acts before Gardevoir’s ordinary attacks but does not reliably KO it; Mega Play Rough threatens Samurott but is not guaranteed through its bulk. Incineroar/Talonflame have previously shown Fake Out/Parting Shot/Wisp/Flare Blitz and Tailwind/Taunt/Wisp/Brave Bird.

decisions.rationale: Flare Blitz guaranteed OHKOs 26% Mawile-Mega (min 61.1%). Ceaseless Edge into 37% Palafin deals 34.8-79.4% with high KO odds plus sets another Spikes layer. If opponent switches Farigiraf into Mawile's slot, Spikes drop it to 22.5% and Flare Blitz still KOs. Incineroar risks a Wave Crash (27.7-102.4%) but OHKO requires an extreme high roll through Sitrus Berry. This line removes Mawile and threatens Palafin simultaneously, securing board advantage.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 decisive. Gardevoir-Mega fainted T3 to Mawile Sucker Punch crit. Opponent's team: Farigiraf (Armor Tail, Trick Room, 35%), Camerupt-Mega (Sheer Force Eruption/Heat Wave/Earth Power), Mawile-Mega (Huge Power, 26%, -1 Atk), Palafin (Zero to Hero, 37%, -1 Atk). Spikes 1 layer on opponent side from Ceaseless Edge. Incineroar Sitrus Berry unactivated. Mawile Play Rough OHKOs Samurott-H with Huge Power even at -1; Flare Blitz always KOs Mawile from 26%. Palafin Wave Crash threatens Incineroar but Sitrus Berry prevents most OHKOs. Camerupt 4x Water weak; Samurott Aqua Cutter always OHKOs. Farigiraf at 35% is fragile with Spikes chip. Kingambit in back with Black Glasses; Sucker Punch blocked when Farigiraf active. Prioritize removing Mawile first, then Palafin, then clean up with Kingambit vs remaining threats.

decisions.rationale: Double Protect safely blanks Incineroar’s first-turn Fake Out and denies Samurott an immediate removal, preserving both damaged attackers for a turn where Incineroar can no longer use Fake Out. Direct offense is too vulnerable to Fake Out plus Samurott pressure, while switching Camerupt into Aqua Cutter is highly dangerous.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s confirmed sets: Timid Mega Gardevoir (Pixilate Hyper Voice/Psyshock/Mystical Fire/Protect), Adamant Sharpness Hisuian Samurott with Chople Berry (Ceaseless Edge/Aqua Cutter/Sacred Sword/Protect), and Impish Intimidate Incineroar (Fake Out/Parting Shot/Will-O-Wisp/Flare Blitz; Sitrus). Unrevealed brought reserve is among Kingambit, Dragapult, Talonflame. Preserve Farigiraf when possible for Armor Tail-supported Trick Room; Mega Camerupt is the preferred Trick Room endgame but must avoid Samurott’s 4x-effective Water attacks. Incineroar’s Fake Out is a central tempo threat on its entry turn; force or absorb it before committing frail attackers.

decisions.rationale: Flare Blitz guaranteed KOs 26% Mawile (min 61%). Ceaseless Edge into 37% Palafin (34.8–79.4%) has a strong KO chance plus Spikes stack. Samurott-H (105) outspeeds Mawile (≤91) so Play Rough can't land before Ceaseless Edge. Palafin Wave Crash into Incineroar does 28–56% and Sitrus Berry keeps it healthy. Worst case Palafin survives low, but Mawile is gone and Palafin is crippled.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 decisive. Gardevoir-Mega fainted T3 to Mawile Sucker Punch crit. Opponent: Farigiraf (Armor Tail, Trick Room, Mental Herb), Camerupt-Mega (Sheer Force Eruption/Heat Wave/Earth Power), Mawile-Mega (Huge Power), Palafin (Zero to Hero, MysticWater). Spikes 1 layer opponent side from Ceaseless Edge. Incineroar Sitrus Berry intact. Kingambit Black Glasses in back; Sucker Punch blocked while Farigiraf active. Camerupt 4x Water weak — Samurott Aqua Cutter always OHKOs. Farigiraf fragile with Spikes chip. Prioritize removing Mawile first, then Palafin, then clean up with Kingambit.

decisions.rationale: Use both priority attacks into Incineroar: Jet Punch preserves Palafin’s remaining HP better than Wave Crash recoil, while Sucker Punch adds damage if Incineroar attacks. Mawile is unlikely to survive the turn, so extract immediate value while retaining Farigiraf for a possible Trick Room endgame.
decisions.notebook: Opponent confirmed: Timid Mega Gardevoir (Pixilate Hyper Voice/Psyshock/Mystical Fire/Protect), Adamant Sharpness Hisuian Samurott with Chople Berry (Ceaseless Edge/Aqua Cutter/Sacred Sword/Protect), and Impish Intimidate Incineroar (Fake Out/Parting Shot/Will-O-Wisp/Flare Blitz; Sitrus Berry). Remaining brought reserve is one of Kingambit, Dragapult, Talonflame. Preserve Farigiraf when possible for Armor Tail-supported Trick Room; Mega Camerupt is preferred in Trick Room but must not face Samurott’s Water attacks. Incineroar’s Fake Out is a central entry-turn tempo threat. Samurott outspeeds Mega Mawile; Palafin outspeeds Incineroar.

decisions.rationale: Deploy both remaining Pokémon; Camerupt preserves the Mega option while Farigiraf’s Armor Tail prevents priority disruption if it survives to establish Trick Room.
decisions.notebook: Opponent confirmed: Timid Mega Gardevoir (Pixilate Hyper Voice/Psyshock/Mystical Fire/Protect), Adamant Sharpness Hisuian Samurott with Chople Berry (Ceaseless Edge/Aqua Cutter/Sacred Sword/Protect), and Impish Intimidate Incineroar (Fake Out/Parting Shot/Will-O-Wisp/Flare Blitz; Sitrus Berry). Remaining brought reserve is one of Kingambit, Dragapult, Talonflame. Preserve Farigiraf when possible for Armor Tail-supported Trick Room; Mega Camerupt is preferred in Trick Room but must avoid Samurott Water attacks. Incineroar’s Fake Out is a central entry-turn tempo threat.

decisions.rationale: Samurott Aqua Cutter into Camerupt: guaranteed OHKO (4x effective, Sharpness, outspeeds). Incineroar Flare Blitz into Farigiraf: guaranteed KO from 11% HP, and +0 priority outruns Trick Room's -7. Both threats eliminated before they act; game and series won.
decisions.notebook: Series won 2-1. Key lessons: Gardevoir-Mega fragile into Mawile-Mega Sucker Punch; Samurott-Hisui Ceaseless Edge Spikes pressure invaluable; Incineroar Intimidate cycling with Parting Shot strong; Kingambit cleans well lategame with Black Glasses; Camerupt-Mega 4x Water weakness exploitable.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Camerupt)
decisions.rationale: Protect preserves Camerupt from Samurott’s guaranteed Aqua Cutter KO while Farigiraf attempts Trick Room. If Samurott targets Camerupt, Trick Room enables Camerupt’s endgame; direct attacks cannot occur before Samurott and lose Camerupt immediately.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s revealed core is Timid Mega Gardevoir, Adamant Sharpness Hisuian Samurott with Chople Berry, and Impish Intimidate Incineroar with Sitrus Berry. Their final brought Pokémon is one of Kingambit, Dragapult, or Talonflame. Samurott’s Aqua Cutter is the immediate 4x threat to Camerupt; preserve Farigiraf where possible to establish Armor Tail-supported Trick Room. Mega Camerupt is the preferred Trick Room win condition. Incineroar Fake Out is blocked against grounded allies by Armor Tail while Farigiraf is active.

decisions.rationale: Samurott-Hisui is guaranteed to move first and Aqua Cutter is a guaranteed KO on Camerupt at its shown HP. Protect can only delay the inevitable because Camerupt remains slower and cannot act before the next Aqua Cutter.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s revealed core: Timid Mega Gardevoir; Adamant Sharpness Hisuian Samurott with Chople Berry; Impish Intimidate Incineroar with Sitrus Berry. Final brought Pokémon was unrevealed among Kingambit, Dragapult, and Talonflame. Samurott’s Aqua Cutter cleanly threatens Camerupt; preserve Armor Tail and establish Trick Room before exposing Camerupt where possible. Mega Camerupt remains the primary Trick Room win condition.

reflections.summary: My between-game adjustment to lead Gardevoir-Mega + Samurott-Hisui won the series because it forced a matchup where Mawile-Mega could not safely set Trick Room; Gardevoir-Mega drew Sucker Punch and fainted, but it enabled Samurott-Hisui to layer Spikes and, alongside Intimidate-cycled Incineroar, wear down the opponent’s slow breakers. Bringing Kingambit over Talonflame was correct as speed control was unnecessary into this Trick-Room-leaning team, and Kingambit’s lategame presence never triggered only because the 4-vs-3 advantage already sealed the game. The prep of Hisuian Samurott with Chople Berry and Ceaseless Edge was the set’s MVP against this opponent’s glaring Fighting/Ground coverage gap and reliance on slow pivots.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series, maintain the same bring—Gardevoir-Mega, Samurott-Hisui, Incineroar, Kingambit—but lead Incineroar + Samurott-Hisui to cycle Intimidate early against Mawile-Mega, secure Spikes immediately, and preserve Gardevoir-Mega for midgame once Mawile-Mega is weakened or removed; set adjustments could replace Protect on Gardevoir-Mega for Taunt to further stifle Trick Room, but the current sets are sufficient.
reflections.notebook: Opponent’s Trick Room core is Mawile-Mega, Farigiraf, Camerupt-Mega; Farigiraf is near-mandatory lead to set Trick Room via Mental Herb + Armor Tail. Mawile-Mega is the primary physical breaker and Sucker Punch threat to Fairy-types. Camerupt-Mega holds Cameruptite and is 4x weak to Water; it often Protects turn 1 to scout. Palafin provides priority Jet Punch and Flip Turn to reset Zero to Hero. Sets to note: Farigiraf carries Mental Herb to guarantee Trick Room; Liepard (Focus Sash, Prankster Fake Out/Thunder Wave/Encore/Taunt) was left in reserve and likely comes against passive leads; Floette-Eternal was not brought but may appear as a Fairy answer. Sharpness Samurott-Hisui with Ceaseless Edge + Aqua Cutter pressures all three Trick Room abusers super-effectively and stacks Spikes which punishes the opponent’s frequent switching; Chople Berry is essential to survive Mawile-Mega’s Sucker Punch or Palafin’s Jet Punch. Incineroar’s Intimidate cycling cripples Mawile-Mega and Palafin; Flare Blitz removes Mawile-Mega and Farigiraf. Gardevoir-Mega forces Mawile-Mega into predictable Sucker Punch patterns and can be traded to keep Samurott-Hisui healthy. Kingambit is a fine cleaner but likely overkill; Talonflame’s Tailwind offers little value against Trick Room.

reflections.summary: The game and 1-2 series were lost primarily because the Game 3 four—Farigiraf, Mega Camerupt, Mega Mawile, and Palafin—could not establish a stable Trick Room position before Samurott-Hisui repeatedly laid Spikes and forced heavy damage. The opening preserved Camerupt but left Mawile and Farigiraf badly weakened; although Mega Mawile's critical Sucker Punch removed Mega Gardevoir, Incineroar plus Samurott then traded efficiently into Palafin and Mawile. With Farigiraf at 11% and no Trick Room established, Camerupt was left alone against Samurott's Aqua Cutter and Incineroar. The between-game direction toward the Farigiraf/Camerupt mode did not pay off here: Armor Tail did not create the needed setup turn, while Samurott's Ceaseless Edge made repeated switching especially costly. Mega Mawile was a reasonable Gardevoir answer and did secure that knockout, but making Mawile the Mega limited the team's endgame once it was worn down; Mega Camerupt was never able to function as the intended Trick Room win condition. Preparation correctly identified Samurott as a major Camerupt threat and brought Farigiraf for priority protection/Trick Room support, but the registered six lacked a robust anti-Spikes, anti-Samurott structure. Heliolisk, Rotom-Fan, and Tauros could plausibly have offered more immediate pressure or positional utility than the slow double-Mega/TR concentration, though no supplied evidence proves any would have solved the matchup. Mega Chandelure may also have offered a more direct Fire-type alternative, but its value cannot be confirmed from the available sets.
reflections.adjustment: For a future series, do not rely on a fragile Farigiraf plus Mega Camerupt endgame when Samurott-Hisui can freely stack Ceaseless Edge. Prioritize immediate pressure on Samurott or a four that does not require repeated switching after Spikes are up. Reassess Mega selection at preview: Mega Mawile is valuable into Mega Gardevoir, but only evolve it if it can be preserved beyond the Gardevoir trade; otherwise build around a different Mega or a faster, less setup-dependent mode. Bring and lead Pokémon that can threaten Samurott while avoiding a passive early sequence, and preserve Farigiraf specifically for a realistic Trick Room turn rather than allowing it to absorb substantial chip before it acts. In roster construction, test Heliolisk, Rotom-Fan, Tauros, or Mega Chandelure against this matchup for clearer Samurott/Incineroar pressure and less dependence on Camerupt.
reflections.notebook: Opponent reliably used Mega Gardevoir + Hisuian Samurott in Game 3. Gardevoir was Timid with Hyper Voice, Psyshock, Mystical Fire, and Protect. Samurott was Adamant Sharpness with Chople Berry, Ceaseless Edge, Aqua Cutter, Sacred Sword, and Protect; it repeatedly used Ceaseless Edge to punish switches and Aqua Cutter is a major Mega Camerupt threat. Incineroar was Impish Intimidate with Sitrus Berry, Fake Out, Parting Shot, Will-O-Wisp, and Flare Blitz; it supports Samurott's chip plan and can cleanly pressure Mega Mawile. The fourth was unrevealed among Kingambit, Dragapult, and Talonflame. Mega Mawile can threaten Mega Gardevoir, but it is vulnerable to the Samurott/Incineroar trade pattern. Do not assume Armor Tail alone guarantees Trick Room; avoid exposing Farigiraf to early chip and avoid repeated switching once Ceaseless Edge is available. Prep should include immediate Samurott pressure and a game plan that is not solely dependent on Mega Camerupt under Trick Room.
